_comment: Who has checked each shell translation, and when.
'baseline' is the English source the other files are translated from.
'unreviewed' means the strings were supplied by a developer or a machine and are
correct to the best of the author's knowledge, but no speaker of the language has
read them. 'reviewed' requires a named person and a date — a translation cannot
review itself, and a tick box with no name behind it is how unchecked wording ends
up in front of a patient.
This governs SHELL text only: buttons, titles, timeouts, error wording. Clinical
content — consent notices, questions, answer options, red-flag wording — is not here.
It lives in the governance registry, needs a qualified practitioner's approval per
language, and is gated by hospital_language.clinically_reviewed. A language can have
a fully reviewed shell and still be unofferable because no notice is published in it.
